i've enjoyed far cry primal for the most part. you definitely can see the skeleton of the last couple of far cry games beneath the surface which is a good thing. it looks great and running around the environment is just as enjoyable as it has been with the last two games.

that being said, there are two major areas that i think suffer from the decision to go with a prehistoric setting. the first is getting around the environment. i was never a big vehicle user in far cry 3 and 4 so i was surprised how much i miss them when playing primal. i also miss being able to fly with the wing suit. however, the lack of vehicles isn't the worst problem.

the major problem has more to do with first person shooters than far cry primal specifically, but the decision to go with the prehistoric setting exacerbates it. close combat and especially melee combat is a puzzle that first person shooters as a genre haven't solved. without the great variety of balistic options the last two far crys have had this game's combat seems repetitive. since combat is a major part of the game i can't help but feel that primal is a brilliant mistake.

So it sounds that it's not a must have even for a fan of the series. I still play far cry 4 and love just roaming the environment. So I can't imagine getting around so much slower without the flight and vehicles. Although riding a sabertooth tiger seems badass!
in spite of my problems with parts of the game i do enjoy it and am not sorry i bought it. however, if i had a choice i would have much rather had a more modern setting for the game.
